dct_description_sm: Berries provide an important source of nutrients and berry picking is an important cultural tradition for people across the Canadian Arctic.  Long-term data addressing the variability in berry productivity and the impacts of ongoing environmental changes on berry producing shrubs is presently lacking. As part of the International Polar Year (IPY) initiative - CiCAT and of ArcticNet, the purpose of this project is to measure the spatial distribution, productivity, and antioxidant levels of four berry producing shrubs in the vicinity of Baker Lake, Nunavut. In addition, vegetation data will be used to ground-truth the vegetation classification put forth in the New Circa-2000 Land Cover map of Northern Canada at 30m Landsat Resolution (Olthof et al. 2008). This research is part of a network of projects currently underway integrating local and traditional ecological knowledge (LTEK) and scientific research to study berry shrub ecology in Nunavut, Nunavik and Nunatsiavut.
